inputs.original_text: Micheál Martin’s claim in Limerick that housing tenancies have increased sounds like carefully chosen cover: point to one reassuring figure while people face rising eviction notices and homelessness under the rules introduced on March 1. Those rules require landlords to provide six-year leases, yet emergency accommodation numbers increased again nationally. The contrast looks less like reassurance than an effort to manage the story while the damage continues.
inputs.modified_text: Martin’s “increased tenancies” line in Limerick looks like a distraction: spotlight one comforting number while eviction notices and homelessness keep rising under the rules introduced on March 1. The six-year lease requirement is being presented as protection, but emergency accommodation numbers have risen nationally again. That contrast doesn’t look accidental—it looks like institutions managing the public story while the harm carries on.
